title: The Nature of Categorical Imperatives
text:
The Categorical Imperative, central to Kantian ethics, serves as a supreme moral law that must be followed unconditionally. It demands an action out of duty rather than inclination or anticipated reward.

The formula dictates that one should only act according to a maxim that can be willed as a universal law without contradiction. If the principle behind an action cannot logically apply to all rational beings in all times, that action is deemed morally impermissible. This approach shifts moral judgment from consequences to the inherent rationality and universality of the will itself.
